faults.quote: commonly used colloquially to mean 'wife' in phrases like benim kadınım
faults.why: Calling one's wife 'kadın' or 'karım' can sound rude/dated; standard polite words are 'eşim' or 'hanımım'.

faults.quote: (family) A married female partner; a wife.
faults.why: Provincial/dated and disrespectful in standard Turkish; teaching it to A2 learners without warning is harmful.
'Kadını' means 'the woman' (accusative) or 'her woman'; 'his wife' would require 'kadınını' (still unnatural).
